description: Introduces activation free energy, catalytic cycles, Michaelis-Menten assumptions, metal and covalent catalysis, and how rate curves, isotope effects, mutants, and structures support mechanistic claims.

related_resources.reason: Enzyme rate models, active sites, catalytic barriers and Michaelis-Menten kinetics.
Protein catalysis, molecular recognition and transition-state stabilization.
ATP and redox carriers, metabolic coupling and reaction energy conservation.
Protein metal-binding sites, redox versus Lewis acid catalysis and metal-dependent enzyme functions.

historical_claims.anchor: An enzyme can lower the relevant activation free energy
historical_claims.source_locator: Catalysis changes reaction rate through alternative lower-barrier paths.
Michaelis parameter is not generally identical to substrate binding Kd.

historical_claims.anchor: Some metalloproteases instead use a metal ion
historical_claims.source_locator: Metal-assisted hydrolysis distinguished from serine-protease mechanism.

historical_claims.anchor: The best mechanistic conclusions survive several independent tests
historical_claims.source_locator: Independent kinetic, structural and chemical evidence for enzyme mechanism.

authorship.scope: Original bioinorganic chemistry and metabolic reaction lectures with source-linked scientific companions and navigation metadata.

background: Basic bonding, reaction free energy, acid-base and oxidation-reduction chemistry; specialized biological cofactors and protein mechanisms are introduced in the narration.
readiness_checks: Why is KM not generally a pure binding affinity?
Why does an inactive mutant not prove a single catalytic assignment?
